chunks: Certainly, many people have turned away from many a (lasting) benefit
for they bent towards the world and spoke with passions
I have been struck with wonder in this matter
upon which people who are self-conceited have agreed
I am providing a cure for their wound but I fear lest it develops into a clot of blood (and becomes incurable)
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the metaphor of the wound turning into a clot of blood in Imam Ali's response to Abu Musa Ashari?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) diagnoses the spiritual malaise of the era, where the shift from divine duty to worldly ambition has led to self-deception among the arbitrators. He employs the medical metaphor of a 'clot' (alaq) to describe a wound that, if left untreated or misdiagnosed due to arrogance, becomes chronic and incurable, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the danger of ego (nafs) in leadership. This context highlights the transition from the ideal governance of the early Caliphate to the pragmatic, often compromised, political realities of the Siffin arbitration.
